q: Does a caprolactam plant emit nitrous oxide?
title: Caprolactam plant N2O emissions
short: Yes. Caprolactam, the raw material for nylon 6, is usually made through hydroxylamine from ammonia oxidation, which forms nitrous oxide. The IPCC 2006 default is 9.0 kg N2O per tonne of caprolactam, about 2.5 tonnes CO2e at a GWP of 273. Report it in Scope 1.
audience: Caprolactam and nylon 6 producers, and their buyers

ul: N2O from the ammonia oxidation step.
CO2 from fuel for steam and process heat.
Electricity for compressors and utilities, in Scope 2.

p: Many routes also make ammonium sulphate, sold as fertiliser. If you share emissions between caprolactam and the by-product, state the rule you used, by mass or by value, and keep it the same each year.
A nylon 6 chip or yarn footprint carries the caprolactam N2O. Ask whether the figure you receive includes it and whether the supplier abates it.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
